charts.title: Shannon's 1951 table against the same statistics on three bodies of text.
charts.takeaway: Single letters and letter pairs match his values within 0.12 bits; his letter-triple value of 3.1 sits 0.39 above ours on old books and 0.23 above ours on Wikipedia.
charts.units: bits per letter (the average number of yes or no questions needed to name the next letter; lower means more predictable text). F1, F2 and F3 are the entropy of a letter given none, one or two letters before it, over 27 symbols
charts.n: three pooled bodies of text, one value per statistic and body
charts.no_interval: Each value is one statistic counted on one pooled body of text. The result file holds no interval.
charts.threshold: Gap to Shannon under 0.15 for F1, 0.2 for F2 and 0.3 for F3, set in advance: failed on old books (F3 gap 0.388), held on Wikipedia (F3 gap 0.228)
charts.planted: Held: the reader missed a known entropy by 0.004 bits

axis.label: bits per letter (lower is more predictable)

charts.title: What each trained reader needs on each kind of text.
charts.takeaway: On its own kind of text (the diagonal) a reader needs 1.63 to 2.41 bits per letter, never Shannon's 1.3; each text is read most cheaply by the reader trained on its own kind, and any other reader costs more, up to 3.78.
charts.units: log loss in bits per letter (the average number of yes or no questions needed to name the next letter; lower means more predictable text). Rows are the text the reader was trained on; columns are the held-out text it read. Brighter cells are higher
charts.n: old fiction: 600,000 training letters, 100,000 held out; fiction, 1892 to 1925: 600,000 training letters, 100,000 held out; The Federalist: 600,000 training letters, 100,000 held out; Wikipedia: 588,712 training letters, 100,000 held out
charts.no_interval: Each cell is one reader scored once on one held-out text. The result file holds no interval.
charts.baseline: Shannon's human reader: about 1.3 bits per letter. Shuffled held-out letters cost this reader 9.26 bits.
charts.threshold: Era penalty larger than genre penalty, set in advance: failed, 0.10 against 0.44

charts.title: What a change of era costs a reader, against a change of genre.
charts.takeaway: Era alone costs 0.10 and 0.25 bits per letter within fiction; genre alone costs 0.44, so genre costs more than era and the claim set in advance failed.
charts.units: transfer penalty in bits per letter: the reader's log loss on the other text minus the log loss of that text's own reader; higher means the change hurt more
charts.n: four trained readers; each text set holds 100,000 held-out characters, of which the second run scored 30,000 letters
charts.no_interval: Each penalty is a difference of two single scores. The result file holds no interval.
charts.baseline: A penalty of 0 means the reader reads the other text as well as its own
charts.threshold: Era penalty larger than genre penalty: failed (0.10 against 0.44). All four forecast bands held.

axis.label: extra bits per letter (higher is a larger cost)

charts.title: Does the reader measure an entropy that is known in advance?
charts.takeaway: Yes: on a made-up letter stream whose true entropy is 2.673 bits, the reader missed by 0.004 bits, far inside the limit of 0.1.
charts.units: absolute error in bits per symbol between the reader's log loss and the true entropy of the planted stream; lower is better
charts.n: one planted stream (a random order-2 Markov chain, where each symbol depends on the two before it)
charts.no_interval: One planted stream, one error. The result file holds no interval.
charts.baseline: True entropy of the planted stream: 2.673 bits per symbol
charts.threshold: Error at most 0.1 bits, set in advance; a larger miss would have voided the study. Held, 0.004
charts.planted: This chart is the planted check

axis.label: error in bits per symbol (lower is better)

rows.label: Reader's miss on the planted stream

charts.title: Real held-out text against the same letters shuffled.
charts.takeaway: Real text costs the reader 2.73 and 1.93 bits per letter; the same letters shuffled cost 8.51 and 9.26, so the reader is using letter order.
charts.units: log loss in bits per letter (the average number of yes or no questions needed to name the next letter; lower means more predictable text)
charts.n: 20 shuffles of the held-out letters in each run
charts.interval: Band: 5th to 95th percentile of the shuffles, with the mean marked
charts.baseline: Control: the held-out text with its letters shuffled, read by the same trained reader
charts.threshold: Real text must cost less than the shuffles' cheapest 5 percent, set in advance: held in both runs

axis.label: bits per letter (lower is more predictable)
